title: South Korea's FSC publishes draft digital asset law making operators liable for hacking losses even without fault
date_note: Both articles are dated 24 November and say the FSC presented the draft at a committee meeting that day.
geo_basis: the FSC, a South Korean government agency, as the articles state
summary: According to Financial News (Yonhap) and Kukmin Ilbo, South Korea's Financial Services Commission made public a government draft law on digital assets on 24 November. Under it, operators would in principle be liable for user losses from hacking or system failures even without intent or negligence, except where the user acted with intent or gross negligence. The draft also provides a basis for a punitive surcharge, capped at 10% of sales, for security failures.
plain: South Korea's financial regulator published a draft law under which crypto businesses would in principle have to compensate users for hacking losses even if the business was not at fault. It is not yet law.
exec: A draft Korean law would make digital asset operators liable for hacking losses without fault, with a punitive surcharge capped at 10% of sales for security failures.

evidence.quote: 징벌적 과징금(최대 매출액의 10%)을 부과할 근거도 마련됐다

validation.note: Financial News (Yonhap wire) and Kukmin Ilbo each state the draft and the no-fault liability. The FSC's own release was not read. fnnews says 10% of total sales; Kukmin Ilbo says revenue.
